pr_title: ESQL: adds Enrich implicit match_fields to field_caps call
pr_body:
This change adds the ENRICH `match_field`s to the field_caps call performed while resolving the index pattern. This addresses scenarios where the match_fields are not explicitly called for in the query and when the index pattern resolution will not use all fields (`*`). A query of the type `from test | enrich countries | keep country_name` doesn't use `ENRICH ... ON ...` (so the field name is not explicitly mentioned) and also asks for a specific field name (thus not using `*` during index pattern resolution).

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/101328
pr_comments: Hi @astefan, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

issue_context.title: ESQL: STATS after ENRICH without KEEP does not work
comments: Could be an overzealous optimization rule that gets rid of the match field `geo.dest`.

Adding an explicit `ON` also works:

```
POST _query?format=txt
{
  "query": """
FROM kibana_sample_data_logs
| ENRICH countries ON geo.dest
| STATS total_bytes = SUM(bytes) BY country_name
| SORT total_bytes DESC
| LIMIT 3
  """
}
```

A simpler query that fails: `FROM test | ENRICH countries | keep number, country_name`. So, it's not about the `stats` command, more about the ENRICH matching field resolution. Being a "hidden" sort-of field and not explicitly present in the query, the matching field (`geo.dest` belonging to the enrich index) resolution fails.

review_comments: Nothing to do with the fix in this PR, but I believe these field names are more clear like this. `-ignoreCsvTests` were suggesting imo that the whole file is ignored in all test suites. In fact, those fields are ignored in CSV unit tests only.
